fixture_meta.purpose: Safety acceptance fixture for Milestone 1 (M1 remediation). Not product. No new legal conclusion: only regimes already verified in VIVAC-TECHNICAL-DISCOVERY.md. Review metadata (review_status, legal/spatial review flags, bitemporal relation) is explicit per remediation F01/F04.
fixture_meta.supersedes: discovery/fixtures/ordesa-feasibility/fixture.json (kept as historical evidence; the packaged copy in alraso/resources is canonical for tests)

review_vocabulary.fragment_review_note: H2/D3: legal_fragment.review_status is a PROVENANCE axis (has the quoted text been checked against its source document?), distinct from rule review. Fragments here were checked against the official texts during discovery, so they carry VERIFIED explicitly; no fixture keeps a private status that production would have to weaken to accept.
review_vocabulary.legal_review_complete: explicit human legal review completed for this version
review_vocabulary.spatial_review_complete: true: scope attribution reviewed; false: pending (never publishable); null: not applicable
review_vocabulary.scope_relevance: H3/D4: REGULATORY (default) means the scope is expected to regulate the modelled activity, so a coverage hole there blocks PERMITTED; CONTEXT_ONLY would be an explicit human declaration that it does not. Both Ordesa scopes are REGULATORY: the park polygon publishes no rule version for these activities in this fixture, so coordinate-mode PERMITTED stays blocked (M1_ORDESA_REAL_WORLD_SPATIAL=NOT_VALIDATED).

hardening_notes.H1: no two visible versions of the same rule_id overlap in valid time here: closures are appended inside the same lineage (same effective_from), never as a competing lineage
hardening_notes.H2: every cited fragment carries a publishable provenance status (VERIFIED)
hardening_notes.H3: both scopes are REGULATORY; the fixture therefore never yields a coordinate-mode PERMITTED
